author: EmanueleCoradin
body:
#### PR description:

`TensorCollection` now derives each tensors size from its SoA, allowing inputs and outputs with different numbers of elements. The new `TensorSlice` selects batches independently for each tensor, providing flexibility needed, for instance, by GNN models.

`BatchedTensorCollection` registers tensors once and manages their per-batch materialization through a new `AlpakaModel::forward()` overload. Tensors can be sliced with individual batch sizes or passed in full to every batch. Full tensors share their handles across batches, reusing writable buffers for const inputs while refreshing their contents before each inference.

Existing inference modules are migrated to the updated interface, with no change to their expected outputs. The README is updated to document the new API and batching semantics.

The new `TrackHitDeepSet` example combines batched track features with full hit features and a hit-to-track mapping. It requires `TrackHitDeepSet.pt` from:
https://github.com/cms-data/PhysicsTools-PyTorchAlpakaTest/pull/2

Thanks to @chrisizeh for reporting this need and providing useful feedback.

#### PR validation:

Added `TrackHitDeepSet` to the PyTorchAlpaka test configuration to exercise tensors with different SoA sizes and mixed full/batched inputs. The default configuration uses 35 tracks with a batch size of 32, exercising a partial final batch.
title: Support per-tensor sizes and more flexible batching in PyTorchAlpaka
